26. 54-year-old woman with a red, painful eye and the patient is complaining of photophobia. When you examine her, you note that visual acuity is decreased in the affected eye and cornea appears opaque and hazy with positive fluoresceine staining. regarding your management, which of the following should be avoided?
explanation_verbatim:
Management to avoid in corneal ulcer → (D) Topical steroid therapy
Steroids delay healing and can worsen corneal infections. The mainstay is topical antibiotics and supportive care.

27. 45-year-old man reports a 2-day history of redness, pain, and photophobia of his left eye. He denies any trauma to the eye, fluoresceine staining reveals dendritic corneal ulcer.
Management would consist of which of the following?
options: Assurance and follow-up in one week
explanation_verbatim: Herpes simplex keratitis is treated with topical antivirals, not steroids. Steroids can exacerbate viral replication.
